comments.author: @ariesdownunder8186
comments.text: Thank you for an amazing video!.  For those complaining about the pronunciation of Hungarian words/towns etc... remember, that Hungarian is one of the hardest languages in the world to learn and pronounce.  Be grateful that people come to make such amazing videos of Hungary - and hey, if you don't like it and you consider yourselves sooo clever  - go out and make your own video

comments.author: @TravelBeyond4K
comments.text: The stunning views along the Danube River and the rolling hills of Tokaj are absolute magic! Hungary has some of the most breathtaking landscapes in all of Central Europe. I could spend endless days soaking in those sunset panoramas!

comments.author: @TravelKismet
comments.text: This footage excellently captures the rustic beauty and profound cultural depth of Hungary. I am truly captivated by how resiliently the locals preserve their unique language and traditional identity through historical ups and downs. Thank you for delivering such an authentic and wonderful perspective on the heart of Europe!

comments.author: @ildikogaspar3421
comments.text: I grew up in Hungary- Tokaj. Living in USA more than 3 decades.  Hearing the name of cities and food pronounced like this is painful- no one will ever understand over there. And I must say, showing red grapes while talking about Tokaj wine is an insult 😂😂😂, sorry!!  The video is a good effort- it’s impossible to show the entire country and the every daily life of ppl in 30 minutes though.

comments.author: @katalinkarpati9276
comments.text: Thank you so so much living in Australia for 3 decades, but my heart and soul still Hungarian. I agree with everything you characterised the Hungarians, but I am very proud  to be born Hungarian and “feel” Hungarian. ❤

replies.author: @TravelBeyond4K
replies.text: That is so sweet to hear! It must be nice seeing your homeland captured so beautifully after living abroad for so long.
